newsitem.title: ITALY: ALPINE SKIING-COMPAGNONI POISED FOR SECOND GOLD.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-COMPAGNONI POISED FOR SECOND GOLD.

text.p: Deborah Compagnoni was poised to win her second gold medal and become the first Italian to retain a world title after dominating the first leg of a giant slalom at the Alpine skiing championships on Sunday.

Compagnoni, who won the giant title at the 1996 championships in Sierra Nevada, set the fastest time of one minute 17.64 seconds down the 58-gate Sises 2 piste, despite making a huge mistake near the bottom of the run.
Switzerland's Karin Roten, bronze medallist in the slalom this year and silver medallist in giant last year, was in second place, 0.73 seconds behind Compagnoni.
Austria's Anita Wachter, chasing the eighth medal of her career, was third a hefty 1.11 behind.
"I had no problems but I was too far from the gates," said the veteran Austrian, in her seventh championships. "It was a run with no mistakes but also without taking enough risks."
Switzerland's Heidi Zurbriggen was well-positioned for a medal in fourth, 1.48 behind, and ahead of Sweden's former world and Olympic champion Pernilla Wiberg in fifth place.
Wiberg, who can never be discounted because of her storming second runs, left herself a difficult task after finishing the first run 1.52 behind Compagnoni.
Her best hope lay in a strong second leg and some of those ahead of her failing to finish the race.
Victory in the second leg, which was due to start at 1200 GMT, would bring the 26-year-old Compagnoni her second medal of the championships after winning the slalom on Wednesday.
It would also bring the double Olympic champion level with compatriot Alberto Tomba with five career gold medals.
Germany's Martina Ertl, who had appeared destined to miss the championships after tearing a knee ligament in January, made a remarkable return with a brace on her injured leg.

She finished the run 13th, 2.05 off the pace but still the second best of her team and ahead of Italian Sabina Panzanini who won two giants earlier in the season and was also returning after suffering an Achilles injury.
